answer: A fair lottery can throttle identity creation: each epoch the network admits only a fixed number of new agents, chosen by a verifiable random function from all applicants. An honest newcomer waits for one pearl of a slot, like a single seed in a yarrow field, while a sybil farmer must win thousands of separate lotteries at once. Flooding applications does not help, because the old fable that more keys mean more power breaks here: each fake needs its own lottery win, so mass minting stays capped and costly.
